The rebase now re-origins the baseline on the incoming session's counters (not zero), so the interleaved A->B->A case no longer double-counts (test_returning_to_an_earlier_session_does_not_double_count_it asserts 1500 not 2700), a resumed session's pre-wave work is excluded (test_new_session_origin_excludes_work_the_wave_did_not_do asserts 61000 not 661000), and a session that ends without a capture folds nothing and does not bump sessions_folded (_fold_finished_session returns base unchanged when latest is None; test_a_session_that_captured_nothing_is_not_counted_as_folded asserts sessions_folded==0). One divergence from criterion 1's literal wording: the carry does NOT record which session ids it folded; RuntimeCarry still carries only an integer sessions_folded, and double-counting is prevented by the re-origin mechanism rather than by a folded-session set. That mechanism is sound (within-session counters are monotonic, so re-originating the baseline forward never re-folds already-counted runtime), but sessions_folded counts stints, not distinct sessions, so a deeper interleave (A->B->A->B) increments it per transition and can over-report distinct sessions folded. This is an audit-trail inaccuracy, not a runtime double-count, so it is a followup rather than a blocker.
